sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: This is part two of the 2017-2018 mini-stories episodes where I interview the staff and our collaborators
sentences.zh: 这是2017-2018年度迷你故事系列的第二部分，我采访了我们的员工和合作者，

sentences.en: about their favorite little design stories that don't quite fill out an entire episode for whatever reason,
sentences.zh: 聊聊他们最喜欢的一些小设计故事，这些故事因为各种原因没能撑起一整集，

sentences.en: but they are cool 99PI stories nonetheless.
sentences.zh: 但它们依然是很棒的《99%隐形》故事。

sentences.en: We have underground tunnels, alarms, mysterious filing cabinets, and gold.
sentences.zh: 我们有地下隧道、警报器、神秘的文件柜，还有黄金。

sentences.en: Tiny, tiny amounts of gold.
sentences.zh: 极少极少量的黄金。

sentences.en: Prepare to be very interesting at your next party.
sentences.zh: 准备好在下次聚会上大显身手吧。

sentences.en: Let's do this.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧。

sentences.en: Why don't you start with who you are, actually?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不先介绍一下你自己呢？

sentences.en: Okay, yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: So I am Delaney Hall, and I am a producer and senior editor on staff.
sentences.zh: 我是德莱尼·霍尔，是这里的制片人和高级编辑。

sentences.en: All right, so what is your story today?
sentences.zh: 好的，那你今天的故事是什么？

sentences.en: Well, first I'm going to introduce you to Peter Sekulowski.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先我要向你介绍彼得·塞库洛夫斯基。

sentences.en: And my levels are okay?
sentences.zh: 我的音量还可以吗？

sentences.en: Okay, so I'm not too loud.
sentences.zh: 好的，我没有太大声吧。

sentences.en: I try to not pop my P's, but I get excited.
sentences.zh: 我尽量不让爆破音太重，但我一兴奋就容易这样。

sentences.en: I'll try not to talk too faSt.
sentences.zh: 我会尽量不说得太快。

sentences.en: And the stuff that Peter gets really excited about, the stuff that makes him pop his P's and talk really fast, is language.
sentences.zh: 而彼得真正兴奋起来，让他说话带爆破音、语速飞快的东西，就是语言。

sentences.en: Because he's the editor-at-large at Merriam-Webster, and he's a lexicographer.
sentences.zh: 因为他是韦氏词典的特约编辑，也是一位词典编纂者。

sentences.en: Lexicographer is a person who compiles and edits dictionaries.
sentences.zh: 词典编纂者就是编写和编辑词典的人。

sentences.en: That's the old definition.
sentences.zh: 那是旧定义了。

sentences.en: And the great Samuel Johnson, the lexicographer in London in the mid-18th century, very famously defined a lexicographer as a harmless drudge.
sentences.zh: 伟大的塞缪尔·约翰逊，那位18世纪中叶伦敦的词典编纂者，曾非常出名地将词典编纂者定义为“无害的苦力”。

sentences.en: And Peter actually said that they use that term affectionately now as like a kind of badge of honor.
sentences.zh: 彼得说，他们现在亲切地使用这个词，把它当作一种荣誉勋章。

sentences.en: They like to be called harmless drudges.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢被称为“无害的苦力”。

sentences.en: So don't worry about insulting them if you want to use that term.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想用这个词，不用担心会冒犯他们。

sentences.en: So what does a harmless drudge like Peter do all day at Merriam-Webster?
sentences.zh: 那么像彼得这样的“无害苦力”在韦氏词典每天都做些什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, from his description, it sounds like they work in an office that is very, very quiet, silent, basically.
sentences.zh: 根据他的描述，听起来他们工作的办公室非常非常安静，基本上是静音的。

sentences.en: And it's filled with these massive steel filing cabinets.
sentences.zh: 里面摆满了巨大的钢制文件柜。

sentences.en: And I've kind of been imagining it like that scene in Raiders of the Lost Ark at the end where the man is pushing that crate through a huge warehouse.
sentences.zh: 我脑海中浮现出的画面就像《夺宝奇兵》结尾那一幕，那个人推着板条箱穿过巨大的仓库。

sentences.en: But instead of stacks of enormous crates, it's filled with metal filing cabinets.
sentences.zh: 但那里堆放的不是巨大的板条箱，而是金属文件柜。

sentences.en: And those metal filing cabinets are filled with index cards.
sentences.zh: 而那些金属文件柜里装满了索引卡片。

sentences.en: As far as I know, it's the largest body of collected evidence of any language in the world.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，这是世界上收集语言证据规模最大的资料库。

sentences.en: It's 15 or 16 million index cards with a word in use, that is to say in context, with its full bibliography.
sentences.zh: 它有1500万到1600万张索引卡片，记录了词汇的使用情况，也就是语境，以及完整的书目信息。

sentences.en: So we know who wrote it and where it was published and when it was published.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道是谁写的，在哪里出版的，以及什么时候出版的。

sentences.en: And so that is the work of lexicographers.
sentences.zh: 这就是词典编纂者的工作。

sentences.en: They're the keepers of that word history.
sentences.zh: 他们是词汇历史的守护者。

sentences.en: And for a long time, before computers came along, this is how they did it with these massive systems of filing cabinets.
sentences.zh: 在计算机出现之前的很长一段时间里，他们就是靠这些庞大的文件柜系统来完成工作的。

sentences.en: There's the file for the phonetician, for the pronunciation editor.
sentences.zh: 那里有语音学家的文件，也就是发音编辑的文件。

sentences.en: There's the file for our dating editors who do the etymological dating.
sentences.zh: 还有负责词源考证的年代编辑的文件。

sentences.en: So it's a place full of file cabinets.
sentences.zh: 所以那是一个到处都是文件柜的地方。

sentences.en: But this isn't actually a story about how the Merriam-Webster offices are filled with filing cabinets.
sentences.zh: 但这其实并不是一个关于韦氏词典办公室里为什么全是文件柜的故事。

sentences.en: It's not, okay.
sentences.zh: 不是的，好吧。

sentences.en: No, it's not.
sentences.zh: 不，不是。

sentences.en: It's a story about one special filing cabinet in their office.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于他们办公室里一个特殊文件柜的故事。

sentences.en: Okay, so here's where it gets really interesting.
sentences.zh: 好了，有趣的地方来了。

sentences.en: So one day, Peter was wandering through these endless rows of filing cabinets, and he came across this one.
sentences.zh: 有一天，彼得在这些无尽的文件柜行间漫步，他偶然发现了这一个。

sentences.en: And one of them simply said, backward index on it.
sentences.zh: 其中一个上面简单地写着“反向索引”。

sentences.en: And so he opens up the cabinet that says backward index.
sentences.zh: 于是他打开了写着“反向索引”的柜子。

sentences.en: And I realized what it was, which was, you know, all of the head words of the Unabridged Dictionary, some 315,000 separate index cards with only one word on them.
sentences.zh: 我意识到那是什么了，你知道，那是《韦氏大词典》所有的词条，大约31.5万张独立的索引卡片，每张卡片上只有一个词。

sentences.en: And it was a head word typed backwards.
sentences.zh: 而且是把词条倒过来拼写的。

sentences.en: And so the head word is the entry in the dictionary.
sentences.zh: 词条就是词典里的条目。

sentences.en: That's the first word.
sentences.zh: 那是第一个词。

sentences.en: That's the word in question.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们要查的词。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是这样。

sentences.en: So this index is like, imagine all the words in the dictionary, but typed backwards and then organized alphabetically.
sentences.zh: 所以这个索引就像是，想象一下词典里所有的词，但都是倒着拼写，然后按字母顺序排列的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So why would you do that?
sentences.zh: 那为什么要这么做呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, that is the question.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这才是问题所在。

sentences.en: Because the utility of it is not immediately obvious, at least not to non-lexicographers like you and me.
sentences.zh: 因为它的用途并不显而易见，至少对你我这样的非词典编纂者来说是这样。

sentences.en: But Peter, the harmless dredge, he kind of got it.
sentences.zh: 但彼得，这个“无害的苦力”，他大概明白了。

sentences.en: Lexicography is an extreme sport.
sentences.zh: 词典编纂是一项极限运动。

sentences.en: This is a kind of a radical practice of collection and of archiving.
sentences.zh: 这是一种激进的收集和归档实践。

sentences.en: And so to a certain degree, this is maybe the weirdest example of that kind of archiving.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，这可能是那种归档方式中最奇怪的例子。

sentences.en: But it made a kind of sense to me.
sentences.zh: 但这对我来说确实有点道理。

sentences.en: And to really understand why it makes any kind of sense, you have to think back to when lexicographers first started compiling the backward index, which was in the 1930s,
sentences.zh: 要真正理解为什么它有道理，你必须回想一下词典编纂者最初开始编制反向索引的时候，那是在20世纪30年代，

sentences.en: it turns out, which was a time before computers.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，那是在计算机出现之前的时代，

sentences.en: and all of the search possibilities that they allow.
sentences.zh: 以及它们所带来的所有搜索可能性。

sentences.en: In the pre-digital era, how else could we have known that there are, for example,
sentences.zh: 在数字时代之前，我们还能怎么知道，比如，

sentences.en: 500 words in the dictionary that end in ology?
sentences.zh: 词典里有500个以“ology”结尾的词呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, you're getting it.
sentences.zh: 对，对，你懂了。

sentences.en: That's because with a regular dictionary just organized in a regular alphabetical way,
sentences.zh: 这是因为在按常规字母顺序排列的普通词典中，

sentences.en: a word like ecology would not appear next to a word like technology
sentences.zh: 像“ecology”（生态学）这样的词不会出现在像“technology”（技术）这样的词旁边，

sentences.en: because one starts with E and one starts with T.
sentences.zh: 因为一个以E开头，一个以T开头。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Okay, so with a backward index,
sentences.zh: 好的，所以有了反向索引，

sentences.en: all the words that end in ology, for example,
sentences.zh: 所有以“ology”结尾的词，比如，

sentences.en: would be grouped together.
sentences.zh: 就会被归在一起。

sentences.en: Yeah, so you couldn't actually look up ology words.
sentences.zh: 没错，所以你其实没法直接查“ology”结尾的词。

sentences.en: You would look up Y-G-O-L-O words.
sentences.zh: 你得查“Y-G-O-L-O”开头的词。

sentences.en: But in doing that, you would find them.
sentences.zh: 但通过这样做，你就能找到它们。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: So cool.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: Kind of ingenious.
sentences.zh: 简直天才。

sentences.en: And there are actually a lot of other examples
sentences.zh: 其实还有很多其他的例子，

sentences.en: of why this is useful.
sentences.zh: 说明它为什么有用。

sentences.en: There was no way that they could know, for example, how many words in English are made with the compound like, like, you know, block-like, clock-like, rock-like, sock-like,
sentences.zh: 他们没法知道，比如，英语中有多少词是用像“like”这样的复合词构成的，比如“block-like”（块状的）、“clock-like”（钟表状的）、“rock-like”（岩石状的）、“sock-like”（袜状的）、

sentences.en: chalk-like, or how many open compounds, that is to say two-word phrases that use pony, so Highland pony, Shetland pony, Welsh pony, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: “chalk-like”（白垩状的），或者有多少开放式复合词，也就是使用“pony”（小马）的双词短语，比如“Highland pony”（高地矮马）、“Shetland pony”（设得兰矮马）、“Welsh pony”（威尔士矮马）之类的。

sentences.en: And then it gets a little deeper, those words that are related morphologically, like ethological, lithological, ornithological, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后更深一层，那些在形态上相关的词，比如“ethological”（行为学的）、“lithological”（岩石学的）、“ornithological”（鸟类学的），你知道，

sentences.en: things that end in that particular sequence of letters.
sentences.zh: 以特定字母序列结尾的词。

sentences.en: And then just basic rhyming sequences, steepy, weepy, sweepy, forty, shorty, snorty.
sentences.zh: 还有基本的押韵序列，“steepy”、“weepy”、“sweepy”、“forty”、“shorty”、“snorty”。

sentences.en: And in fact, this backward index was instrumental in the creation of Merriam-Webster's first rhyming dictionary.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这个反向索引在韦氏词典第一本押韵词典的创作中起到了关键作用。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是吗。

sentences.en: I have one of those.
sentences.zh: 我有一本。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: They're still, they're very popular.
sentences.zh: 它们现在仍然非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: They're really, really good.
sentences.zh: 它们真的非常非常棒。

sentences.en: So by reading words backwards, you can start to see new kinds of patterns like the ology pattern or the logical pattern or just rhyming patterns.
sentences.zh: 所以通过倒着读单词，你可以开始看到新的模式，比如“ology”模式或“logical”模式，或者仅仅是押韵模式。

sentences.en: That's so cool.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: The kind of lexical detail that we can get into by looking at the language backwards does sort of illuminate our knowledge of the language as we read it in a normal way.
sentences.zh: 通过倒着看语言所能获得的词汇细节，确实照亮了我们以正常方式阅读时对语言的认知。

sentences.en: So you said it came from the 1930s before there were computers, but does Peter know anything about who actually made this mysterious fallen cabinet?
sentences.zh: 你说它来自20世纪30年代，在计算机出现之前，但彼得知道是谁制作了这个神秘的文件柜吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 知道。

sentences.en: So after he discovered it, he started doing some research.
sentences.zh: 在他发现它之后，他开始做一些研究。

sentences.en: And exactly who invented it is still a bit of a mystery.
sentences.zh: 到底是谁发明的，现在还是个谜。

sentences.en: He figured out that it dates back to the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 他查出它追溯到20世纪30年代。

sentences.en: And there's some evidence that lexicographers worked on it up until the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 而且有证据表明，词典编纂者一直工作到20世纪70年代。

sentences.en: So he knows how long it was actively being compiled.
sentences.zh: 所以他知道它被积极编制了多久。

sentences.en: And he also found out that the project was a kind of favorite pet project of this one editor named Philip Gove.
sentences.zh: 他还发现这个项目是编辑菲利普·戈夫最钟爱的项目。

sentences.en: He edited Webster's third unabridged dictionary in the 1950s, and it sounds like he was very rigorous and rule-oriented.
sentences.zh: 他在20世纪50年代编辑了《韦氏第三版大词典》，听起来他非常严谨，注重规则。

sentences.en: Who is sort of famous for his organizational skills and for making the dictionary apparatus, that is to say, the things that we use as kind of code in the dictionary.
sentences.zh: 他以组织能力和制定词典体系而闻名，也就是我们作为词典代码使用的那些东西。

sentences.en: Things like, you know, what does a bold-faced colon mean?
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道，粗体的冒号是什么意思？

sentences.en: What does a light-faced, you know, italic semicolon mean?
sentences.zh: 细体的斜体分号是什么意思？

sentences.en: When can we use commas?
sentences.zh: 什么时候可以用逗号？

sentences.en: There's a rule for everything.
sentences.zh: 凡事都有规则。

sentences.en: And so it was really Gove who systematized all of that.
sentences.zh: 所以确实是戈夫将这一切系统化了。

sentences.en: He made a rule book for us, for the editors, that was followed to the T.
sentences.zh: 他为我们，为编辑们制定了一本规则手册，必须严格遵守。

sentences.en: It was really, really strict and very kind of innovative in its way and also kind of proto-digital
sentences.zh: 它真的非常非常严格，而且在当时非常创新，也算是一种原始数字化的尝试，

sentences.en: because when we finally did digitize that dictionary, we recognized how very regular the apparatus was.
sentences.zh: 因为当我们最终将那本词典数字化时，我们意识到这个体系是多么规范。

sentences.en: So Gove, from Peter's description, it seems like he thought about the dictionary with the logic of a computer programmer,
sentences.zh: 所以根据彼得的描述，戈夫似乎是用计算机程序员的逻辑来思考词典的，

sentences.en: but before computers were a thing.
sentences.zh: 但在计算机还没出现的时候。

sentences.en: And now that computers are a thing, I mean, you mentioned the backward index sort of fell out in the 1970s, which makes tons of sense.
sentences.zh: 既然现在有了计算机，我的意思是，你提到反向索引在20世纪70年代左右就没落了，这非常合理。

sentences.en: The computers must have really changed the way lexicographers or the dictionary really works.
sentences.zh: 计算机一定彻底改变了词典编纂者或词典的工作方式。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全改变了。

sentences.en: I mean, for one thing, they have made the old school backwards index totally obsolete.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，首先，它们让老派的反向索引完全过时了。

sentences.en: On the Merriam-Webster website, there's an advanced search function where you can type in ology or phobia.
sentences.zh: 在韦氏词典网站上，有一个高级搜索功能，你可以输入“ology”或“phobia”。

sentences.en: And you don't have to spell it backwards.
sentences.zh: 你不需要倒着拼写。

sentences.en: No, you don't have to spell it backwards.
sentences.zh: 不，你不需要倒着拼写。

sentences.en: It pulls up all the words that end with ology or phobia.
sentences.zh: 它会调出所有以“ology”或“phobia”结尾的词。

sentences.en: So easy.
sentences.zh: 太简单了。

sentences.en: We have it so easy.
sentences.zh: 我们现在太轻松了。

sentences.en: We really do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: We really do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And then computers have also allowed lexicographers like Peter to see other kinds of interesting patterns.
sentences.zh: 而且计算机也让像彼得这样的词典编纂者能够看到其他有趣的模式。

sentences.en: For example?
sentences.zh: 比如？

sentences.en: Well, my favorite that we talked about in this interview is this function on Merriam-Webster's website, which is called Time Traveler.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在这次采访中谈到的我最喜欢的功能是韦氏词典网站上的一个功能，叫做“时间旅行者”。

sentences.en: By which you can reorder the dictionary in chronological order as opposed to alphabetical order because ultimately alphabetical order is random.
sentences.zh: 通过它，你可以按时间顺序而不是字母顺序重新排列词典，因为归根结底，字母顺序是随机的。

sentences.en: It's arbitrary.
sentences.zh: 它是随意的。

sentences.en: But chronological order isn't because English develops in a very particular way.
sentences.zh: 但时间顺序不是，因为英语的发展方式非常独特。

sentences.en: All the words, for example, about train travel and train tracks and coal and engines, they all come at a certain time.
sentences.zh: 所有的词，比如关于火车旅行、铁轨、煤炭和引擎的词，它们都在特定的时间出现。

sentences.en: All words that have to do with repeating firearms, they all come at a certain time.
sentences.zh: 所有与连发枪支有关的词，它们都在特定的时间出现。

sentences.en: You know, the words that entered the language regarding the law that are derived from French, they all come in at a similar time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些源自法语的法律词汇，它们都在相似的时间进入语言。

sentences.en: So reorganizing the dictionary in a digital way turns out to be a way to sort of turn the dictionary into a three-dimensional search rather than just simply a list we can go in greater depth.
sentences.zh: 所以以数字方式重新组织词典，结果变成了一种将词典转化为三维搜索的方式，而不是仅仅作为一个列表，我们可以进行更深入的研究。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: Isn't that fascinating?
sentences.zh: 这不迷人吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I know what alchemy is.
sentences.zh: 我知道什么是炼金术。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: What is it?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: It is the idea of using chemistry to turn lead into gold.
sentences.zh: 就是利用化学方法把铅变成金子的想法。

sentences.en: Yeah, basically.
sentences.zh: 对，基本上是这样。

sentences.en: Or any other base metal.
sentences.zh: 或者任何其他贱金属。

sentences.en: It was this loony idea that folks in the medieval ages were obsessed with,
sentences.zh: 这是中世纪人们痴迷的一种疯狂想法，

sentences.en: turning base metals like lead or mercury into gold,
sentences.zh: 把铅或汞之类的贱金属变成金子，

sentences.en: which, of course, is preposterous nowadays.
sentences.zh: 当然，这在今天看来是荒谬的。

sentences.en: But there's this time when alchemists were these like really dope people backed by rich folks and powerful folks, including King Henry IV of France.
sentences.zh: 但曾有一段时间，炼金术士是非常了不起的人，他们有富人和权贵的支持，包括法国国王亨利四世。

sentences.en: A lot of Catholic monks practice alchemy.
sentences.zh: 许多天主教僧侣也钻研炼金术。

sentences.en: Even Sir Isaac Newton was super into alchemy.
sentences.zh: 甚至艾萨克·牛顿爵士也对炼金术非常着迷。

sentences.en: He apparently wrote about it more than physics and optics.
sentences.zh: 据说他写下的关于炼金术的内容比物理学和光学还要多。

sentences.en: So for a long time, hundreds and hundreds of years across the entire world in the Middle East and Europe, there were these blurred lines between science and alchemy.
sentences.zh: 所以很长一段时间里，在世界各地的中东和欧洲，科学与炼金术之间的界限一直很模糊，持续了数百年之久。

sentences.en: In fact, alchemy can actually be traced back to the Arabic alchemy, which means chemistry, because apparently Egyptians were pretty big into alchemy back in the day,
sentences.zh: 事实上，炼金术可以追溯到阿拉伯语的“炼金术”，意思就是化学，因为显然埃及人在当时就非常热衷于炼金术，

sentences.en: especially during the Hellenistic times in Alexandria, which is where I used to live.
sentences.zh: 特别是在亚历山大港的希腊化时期，那也是我曾经住过的地方。

sentences.en: So shout out to Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 所以向亚历山大港致敬。

sentences.en: And so alchemy was this really big thing, and it is still really prevalent in pop culture today.
sentences.zh: 炼金术曾经是一件大事，而且在今天的流行文化中依然非常普遍。

sentences.en: Like, I don't know if your kids play like Minecraft or World of Warcraft.
sentences.zh: 比如，我不知道你的孩子们玩不玩《我的世界》或《魔兽世界》之类的游戏。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然玩。

sentences.en: Based on a cursory Google search, I think there are some alchemist characters involved in those.
sentences.zh: 根据简单的谷歌搜索，我想里面确实有一些炼金术士角色。

sentences.en: And one of the examples from my childhood is in Harry Potter.
sentences.zh: 我童年的一个例子就是《哈利·波特》。

sentences.en: The whole first book is about the Sorcerer's Stone or in the British version, the Philosopher's Stone,
sentences.zh: 第一本书讲的就是“魔法石”，或者在英国版本里叫“贤者之石”，

sentences.en: which is this thing that turns metals into gold and also apparently makes people immortal, which is why Voldemort was all about it.
sentences.zh: 这东西能把金属变成金子，据说还能让人长生不老，这就是为什么伏地魔对它如此执着。

sentences.en: I'm sorry, he must not be named, was all about it.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，是那个“连名字都不能提的人”对它如此执着。

sentences.en: Um, anyway, that's all to say that this idea that you could design or, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，总之，这就是说，那种认为你可以设计，或者说，你知道，

sentences.en: kind of design gold from other metals was a really big pseudoscientific quest for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 从其他金属中设计出金子的想法，在很长一段时间里是一个非常重大的伪科学追求。

sentences.en: But that all sort of went by the wayside when modern chemistry started to become its own discipline, you know,
sentences.zh: 但当现代化学开始成为一门独立的学科时，这一切就逐渐被淘汰了，你知道，

sentences.en: with atoms and neutrons and electrons and all that stuff sort of started taking hold.
sentences.zh: 随着原子、中子、电子等概念开始占据主导地位。

sentences.en: Well, the ironic thing is, is that with modern chemistry, it is actually possible to create gold from other elements.
sentences.zh: 嗯，讽刺的是，有了现代化学，实际上是有可能从其他元素制造出金子的。

sentences.en: It actually happens in nature, like when neutron stars collide, and it can happen in labs if you have nuclear capabilities or like a particle accelerator,
sentences.zh: 这在自然界中确实会发生，比如当中子星碰撞时，如果你有核能力或者像粒子加速器这样的设备，在实验室里也能做到，

sentences.en: which brings us to Maryland in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带到了20世纪60年代的马里兰州。

sentences.en: There was a physicist there named Judith Temperley, and there with a nuclear reactor, she managed to turn mercury into gold.
sentences.zh: 那里有一位名叫朱迪思·坦珀利的物理学家，她利用核反应堆成功地将汞变成了金子。

sentences.en: Well, she actually transmuted it, which is a technical term.
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上她是进行了“嬗变”，这是一个专业术语。

sentences.en: And as I understand it, it means she modified the nucleus of one element until it had the same amount of protons as gold.
sentences.zh: 据我理解，这意味着她修改了一种元素的原子核，直到它拥有与金子相同数量的质子。

sentences.en: Should I do a quick chemistry lesson?
sentences.zh: 我要来个简短的化学课吗？

sentences.en: I mean, go for it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，请便。

sentences.en: Okay, cool.
sentences.zh: 好的，酷。

sentences.en: So a quick chemistry lesson.
sentences.zh: 那么，简短的化学课。

sentences.en: Elements are defined by the number of protons in their nucleus.
sentences.zh: 元素是由其原子核中的质子数定义的。

sentences.en: Like hydrogen is number one in the periodic table, which means it has one proton in its nucleus.
sentences.zh: 比如氢在元素周期表中排第一，意味着它的原子核里有一个质子。

sentences.en: Sodium is number 11.
sentences.zh: 钠是第11号元素。

sentences.en: It has 11 protons, so on, so on.
sentences.zh: 它有11个质子，以此类推。

sentences.en: Um, so the idea was that if you got an element that had, you know, close to the number of protons as gold, um, then maybe like with a particle accelerator,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以想法是，如果你找到一种元素，它的质子数接近金子，嗯，那么也许用粒子加速器，

sentences.en: you could add protons to it or strip protons away.
sentences.zh: 你可以给它增加质子或者剥离质子。

sentences.en: But to do that, you need a huge amount of energy because if you collide two positive things, which protons are, then they would like bounce off each other.
sentences.zh: 但要做到这一点，你需要巨大的能量，因为如果你让两个带正电的东西（质子就是带正电的）碰撞，它们会互相弹开。

sentences.en: So you need a particle accelerator to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要粒子加速器来完成。

sentences.en: And mercury is number 80 on the periodic table of elements.
sentences.zh: 汞在元素周期表上是第80号元素。

sentences.en: Gold is number 79.
sentences.zh: 金子是第79号。

sentences.en: So they're very close.
sentences.zh: 所以它们非常接近。

sentences.en: So she was like, OK, cool.
sentences.zh: 所以她想，好的，酷。

sentences.en: I'll put mercury in there, which has 80 protons.
sentences.zh: 我把汞放进去，它有80个质子。

sentences.en: I'll try to smack one of those off and maybe one of the protons will fall off and I'll be left with gold.
sentences.zh: 我试着撞掉其中一个，也许其中一个质子会掉下来，剩下的就是金子了。

sentences.en: And she did that.
sentences.zh: 她确实做到了。

sentences.en: She, I think, successfully converted one atom into gold, which, you know, great.
sentences.zh: 我想她成功地将一个原子转化成了金子，这，你知道，很棒。

sentences.en: That was a really great job.
sentences.zh: 那是一项非常伟大的工作。

sentences.en: And she proved that this idea that was really crazy but was so obsessed over for so many hundreds of years was actually scientifically possible.
sentences.zh: 她证明了这个曾经被认为非常疯狂、却被人们痴迷了数百年的想法，在科学上确实是可能的。

sentences.en: And then in the 1980s, this professor named Glenn T.
sentences.zh: 然后在20世纪80年代，一位名叫格伦·T·西博格的教授，

sentences.en: Seaborg, who was a Nobel winning chemist at Berkeley, made even more gold, transmuted it the same way.
sentences.zh: 他是伯克利分校的诺贝尔奖化学家，制造了更多的金子，用同样的方法进行了嬗变。

sentences.en: Except this time he used bismuth, which, you know, unlike mercury, isn't poisonous.
sentences.zh: 只不过这次他用了铋，你知道，和汞不同，铋没有毒。

sentences.en: And it was also pretty close to gold on the periodic table.
sentences.zh: 而且它在元素周期表上离金子也很近。

sentences.en: I think it was 83 protons, number 83, compared to gold 79.
sentences.zh: 我想它有83个质子，是83号元素，而金子是79号。

sentences.en: So he smacked some carbon into it using a particle accelerator, and he managed to create several thousand atoms of gold.
sentences.zh: 所以他用粒子加速器把一些碳撞进铋里，成功制造出了几千个金原子。

sentences.en: You know, in both cases, the end results were sort of invisible, like to the naked eye.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在这两种情况下，最终的结果用肉眼看都是不可见的。

sentences.en: So it doesn't seem like the best option for creating wealth.
sentences.zh: 所以这看起来并不是创造财富的最佳选择。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Especially considering that you need a particle accelerator, which I hear is pretty expensive to build.
sentences.zh: 特别是考虑到你需要一个粒子加速器，我听说建造它非常昂贵。

sentences.en: So this centuries-long quest becomes possible, but in the end,
sentences.zh: 所以这个持续了几个世纪的追求变得可能了，但最终，

sentences.en: it's pretty impractical because you really have to spend way more gold than could ever be made creating a gold atom out of bismuth.
sentences.zh: 它非常不切实际，因为你从铋中制造一个金原子所花费的成本，远远超过了所能制造出的金子的价值。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: I think Seaborg the chemist told the Associated Press at the time that in order to create an ounce of gold using his process that he did in Berkeley,
sentences.zh: 我想化学家西博格当时告诉美联社，为了用他在伯克利使用的方法制造出一盎司金子，

sentences.en: it would take one quadrillion dollars to create an ounce of gold.
sentences.zh: 制造一盎司金子需要花费一千万亿（Quadrillion）美元。

sentences.en: And I had to look up Quadrillion.
sentences.zh: 我不得不去查了一下“千万亿”这个词。

sentences.en: It's a one with 15 zeros after it.
sentences.zh: 就是一个1后面跟着15个零。

sentences.en: And at the same time, the going rate for gold was about $560 an ounce.
sentences.zh: 而当时金子的市场价格大约是每盎司560美元。

sentences.en: So not the most cost effective, but pretty cool that we did it.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是最划算的，但我们能做到这一点还是很酷的。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Last, but certainly not least, is the longest serving soldier in the 99 PI Army, Avery Truffleman.
sentences.zh: 最后，但同样重要的一位，是99 PI军团中服役时间最长的士兵，艾弗里·特拉夫曼。

sentences.en: I want to start with a question for you.
sentences.zh: 我想先问你一个问题。

sentences.en: So how long have you lived in the Bay Area?
sentences.zh: 你在湾区住了多久了？

sentences.en: I moved here in 1997.
sentences.zh: 我是1997年搬到这里的。

sentences.en: So are there any tourist attractions that you still haven't been to?
sentences.zh: 那么有什么旅游景点是你还没去过的吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，有啊。

sentences.en: Let me think.
sentences.zh: 让我想想。

sentences.en: Alcatraz, Pier 39, Lombard Street.
sentences.zh: 恶魔岛、39号码头、伦巴底街。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: I've never driven down Lombard Street.
sentences.zh: 我从来没开车走过伦巴底街。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 真的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's so funny that you would love Lombard Street.
sentences.zh: 你会喜欢伦巴底街真是太有趣了。

sentences.en: Well, okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧。

sentences.en: So I grew up in New York, lived there for my whole childhood and adulthood or youthhood.
sentences.zh: 我是在纽约长大的，整个童年和成年期或者青年期都住在那里。

sentences.en: And I never, ever went to the crown of the Statue of Liberty.
sentences.zh: 但我从来、从来没有去过自由女神像的皇冠处。

sentences.en: And now it's too late.
sentences.zh: 现在已经太晚了。

sentences.en: And it was the kind of thing that everyone always told me to do.
sentences.zh: 那件事每个人都一直劝我去做。

sentences.en: And it's, you know, just kind of a typical thing that locals have a very different experience of their town and their city than visitors.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是一种很典型的现象，当地人对他们城镇和城市的体验与游客完全不同。

sentences.en: Because by and large, they don't see the attractions.
sentences.zh: 因为总的来说，他们不会去看那些景点。

sentences.en: The vast majority of our visitors are from out of town.
sentences.zh: 我们绝大多数游客都是外地来的。

sentences.en: Overwhelming majority.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数。

sentences.en: Think about locals doing tourist activities in any town around the United States.
sentences.zh: 想想看美国任何城镇的当地人做游客活动的情况。

sentences.en: Many people do not go to the tourist thing in their town.
sentences.zh: 很多人都不会去他们镇上的旅游景点。

sentences.en: This is Dean Najarian.
sentences.zh: 这位是迪恩·纳贾里安。

sentences.en: He is a tour guide in an area of downtown Seattle called Pioneer Square.
sentences.zh: 他是西雅图市中心一个叫先锋广场地区的导游。

sentences.en: It's very touristy.
sentences.zh: 那里非常受游客欢迎。

sentences.en: and he works for a company called Bill Spidell's Underground Tour.
sentences.zh: 他为一家叫“比尔·斯派德尔地下之旅”的公司工作。

sentences.en: And as the name suggests, the tour allows you to descend some steps
sentences.zh: 顾名思义，这个旅游项目让你走下一些台阶，

sentences.en: and find yourself below street level.
sentences.zh: 然后发现自己身处街道下方。

sentences.en: Like literally underground.
sentences.zh: 就像字面意思上的地下。

sentences.en: Under the ground.
sentences.zh: 在地面之下。

sentences.en: I lived here for 12 years before I knew about it.
sentences.zh: 我在这里住了12年才知道这个地方。

sentences.en: It's safe to say easily the majority of people who live and work in Seattle
sentences.zh: 可以肯定地说，在西雅图生活和工作的人中，绝大多数人

sentences.en: do not know this.
sentences.zh: 都不知道这一点。

sentences.en: They don't know that as we look around up above there,
sentences.zh: 他们不知道当我们抬头看上面的时候，

sentences.en: that all of the sidewalks you see up there,
sentences.zh: 你看到的所有人行道，

sentences.en: all of those sidewalks are hollow.
sentences.zh: 所有那些人行道都是中空的。

sentences.en: What does he mean that the sidewalks are hollow?
sentences.zh: 他说的“人行道是中空的”是什么意思？

sentences.en: To explain that, we have to go back to 1851, to the founding of Seattle when the first white settlers arrived.
sentences.zh: 要解释这一点，我们得回到1851年，回到西雅图建城时，当时第一批白人定居者抵达这里。

sentences.en: And back then, the land looked completely different, like topographically.
sentences.zh: 那时，这片土地的地形看起来完全不同。

sentences.en: It was, I mean, shockingly different.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，简直是天差地别。

sentences.en: If you look at a map, Seattle was this tiny little peninsula that used to sometimes flood into an island periodically.
sentences.zh: 如果你看地图，西雅图曾经是一个小小的半岛，有时会周期性地被淹没成一座岛屿。

sentences.en: And it was not the best place to establish a city.
sentences.zh: 那并不是建立城市的最佳地点。

sentences.en: But some young white guys went ahead and established it.
sentences.zh: 但一些年轻的白人小伙子还是执意建立了它。

sentences.en: And Pioneer Square quickly became this little logging town full of tiny wooden houses and a logging mill.
sentences.zh: 先锋广场很快就变成了一个充满小木屋和伐木厂的伐木小镇。

sentences.en: That was the original Pioneer Square area.
sentences.zh: 那就是最初的先锋广场地区。

sentences.en: And that's where the dock was.
sentences.zh: 码头就在那里。

sentences.en: That's where some of the early businesses were.
sentences.zh: 早期的一些企业也在那里。

sentences.en: This is historian Alan Stein.
sentences.zh: 这位是历史学家艾伦·斯坦。

sentences.en: And he says even after the settlement, the town would still flood sometimes.
sentences.zh: 他说即使在定居之后，这个城镇有时仍然会发大水。

sentences.en: And this meant plumbing was impossible.
sentences.zh: 这意味着管道系统根本无法使用。

sentences.en: The toilets were at sea level.
sentences.zh: 厕所就在海平面上。

sentences.en: So the problem is any time the tide came in, it would blast water through.
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，每当潮水上涨时，它就会把水冲进来。

sentences.en: And so, you know, these toilets erupting with water.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这些厕所会喷出水来。

sentences.en: Well, that just sounds awful.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那听起来真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, it was a stupid place to establish a town.
sentences.zh: 噢，没错，把城镇建在那儿真是个愚蠢的决定。

sentences.en: It was a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 那是个糟糕的主意。

sentences.en: But the settlers decided to grin and bear it,
sentences.zh: 但定居者们决定忍气吞声，

sentences.en: and they put up with the many faults of their little city
sentences.zh: 他们忍受着这座小城带来的诸多弊端，

sentences.en: as long as they could continue to sell its lumber
sentences.zh: 只要能继续卖木材就行，

sentences.en: until they accidentally burned the entire city to the ground.
sentences.zh: 直到他们不小心把整座城市烧成了灰烬。

sentences.en: And when the Great Fire hit in 89, that burned down.
sentences.zh: 当 89 年那场大火袭来时，一切都烧毁了。

sentences.en: That started at Pioneer Square.
sentences.zh: 火是从先锋广场开始的。

sentences.en: that burned down most of that area because by this time, wooden buildings had been built up.
sentences.zh: 那场大火烧毁了大部分地区，因为当时已经建起了木质建筑。

sentences.en: In 1889, the Great Fire hits Seattle, and it just pretty much levels downtown.
sentences.zh: 1889 年，大火席卷西雅图，几乎把市中心夷为平地。

sentences.en: It's just destroyed.
sentences.zh: 它被彻底摧毁了。

sentences.en: But miraculously, no one died in the Great Fire.
sentences.zh: 但奇迹般的是，大火中无人丧生。

sentences.en: So the city actually sees this as an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 所以，城市实际上把这看作是一个机会。

sentences.en: Seattle's like, okay, this is our big chance to get the town above sea level, and we can start again.
sentences.zh: 西雅图人想，好吧，这是我们把城镇抬高到海平面以上的大好机会，我们可以重新开始。

sentences.en: They thought, well, let's grade it over.
sentences.zh: 他们想，嗯，让我们把它垫高吧。

sentences.en: Let's pack up the streets so that they're 11 feet higher in the air.
sentences.zh: 把街道填高，让它们比原来高出 11 英尺。

sentences.en: and that way it's a little more stable.
sentences.zh: 这样会更稳固一些。

sentences.en: But the business owners had already started building.
sentences.zh: 但商户们已经开始动工建设了。

sentences.en: The city didn't want to tell the businesses in Pioneer Square
sentences.zh: 市政府不想告诉先锋广场的商户们，

sentences.en: to wait until the project was done to rebuild
